No builds, tests, syntax checks, GPU work, profilers, process inspection, Git, cleanup, Orca calls, worker contact, or product edits.

comparison_metadata.finding_used: R841 recommended R842 as a distinct command-DAG capture/replay archive and R843 as a decision-support source audit tied to the current typed-QSA regression.
Prior round metadata distinguishes R786's graph traversal/destination-aggregation topic from GPU command-graph replay. R817 metadata concerns binary/ISA extraction, not event-time attribution.

current_context_supplied_by_parent.status: Nine clean 39K processes remain the performance cohort: FP32 median 372.5, vLLM BF16 394.9, typed QSA 384.8 tok/s. A natural 32K four-arm numerical screen is active and source/binary frozen at 6354. R844 is a separate source-only exact-normal exponent fastpath proposal and remains active. Main reports the newer coarse profile's old-attention 33.9610 s versus typed-attention 36.2963 s, projection 0.919497 s versus 1.20636 s, and explicit-wait-excluded CPU 19.124 s versus 19.193 s; queue windows are nonexclusive.

measurement_records.interpretation_limit: The receipt labels diagnostic queue intervals nonexclusive and inclusive of host submission gaps. They are not exclusive device service fractions.

scope_depth.judgment: Strong, coherent completion of R841's recommended scope. At 1,574 words it is within the 1,300–1,700 budget; seven unique primary URLs meet the seven-source cap. The report compares CUDA capture/replay and updates with experimental SYCL graph support, uses a whole-loop break-even model, and includes multiple measured regimes and explicit evidence limits.
scope_depth.evidence: The V100 example separates device kernel duration from end-to-end submission timing and first removes per-kernel synchronization before attributing the smaller remaining gain to graphs. The A100 study includes creation cost, graph size and replay-count crossover. IWOCL results include an A770 small-workload win and a PVC 1100 large-workload result with only 3% aggregate gain.
scope_depth.limits: The CUDA and Intel measurements are tied to their named systems and test stacks. The SYCL extension and DPC++ design pages are experimental/current-source documentation, not proof of support on this B570. None of these results establishes Strata graph support or a local launch bottleneck.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Distinct from R811/R832/R835/R839's messages, pipeline/barrier, stencil/halo, and local-bank-layout topics. It follows R841's evidence-based scope recommendation.
novelty_and_redundancy.metadata_overlap_checked: R786 metadata mentions historical CUDA graph studies among sources, but its subject is sparse graph traversal and destination aggregation; this is not command-DAG replay. R842's capture/build/replay/update amortization remains a new, coherent topic.
novelty_and_redundancy.conclusion: Retain as a reusable command-graph knowledge archive; do not infer an adoption case from it.

primary_source_verification.status: Material version, measurement-boundary, and API-maturity claims were checked against primary sources.

verified.claim: The V100/CUDA 10.1 example reports a 2.9 microsecond device kernel; host-wall-clock loop values of 9.6 microseconds with synchronization per kernel, 3.8 microseconds with synchronization per 20-kernel step, and 3.4 microseconds with graph replay; capture plus instantiation is about 400 microseconds.

The pinned v1 paper identifies A100 40 GB, CUDA 12.3 and driver 545.23.08; it reports graph creation/upload growing with node count, a useful batch around 50–100 kernels and a two-to-three batch crossover for the smallest tested workload.

Slides identify the A770 driver/DPC++/oneMKL configuration, report the small A770 3k case near 2x, and report only 3% for the Data Center GPU Max 1100 192k case. The deck also shows approximately 3 ms FFT steps in that latter case.
The guide distinguishes definition, instantiation and replay; documents stream capture and explicit construction; and describes graph update constraints and node-level updates.
DPC++ documentation describes command-buffer support as experimental and exposes limited/full graph device aspects.

The experimental extension says native recording hides node/edge details and does not support executable graph update; feature support depends on the backend. This URL tracks the sycl branch, so its retrieval date is part of provenance.

corrections.issue: R842 says the IWOCL slides attribute the PVC 1100 192k case's flat 3% result to GPU-kernel-bound work.
corrections.correction: The slides confirm the 3% result and show some roughly 3 ms FFT steps, but the P55 text says the trace has no long GPU-state-copy waits and describes the performance as not GPU-bound. The cited source does not support the report's GPU-bound attribution. Preserve the measurement and state the cause as unresolved unless the source wording is reconciled.
corrections.source_location: IWOCL PDF, pages 54–55 (zero-based pages 53–54), especially the PVC 192k slide.

provenance_and_applicability.implementation_source: No code, helper, diagnostic, or test was copied or proposed. Public CUDA/Intel documentation, an original arXiv study, and IWOCL presentation measurements are summarized.
unqualified: No Arc B570/Xe2 command-graph capability, update support, runtime behavior, or performance is established.
No local Strata bottleneck, end-to-end gain, or adoption decision is established.

retrieval.retrieve_when: A closed Main profile establishes that repeated host submission gaps materially limit a stable command DAG, and the actual B570 runtime/device graph aspects and command eligibility are checked.
retrieval.main_correction_to_retain: Do not repeat the report's GPU-bound explanation for the PVC 192k result; the cited slide supports only the 3% measurement and its displayed trace/timings. Do not infer B570 support or performance from A770/PVC.

scope_depth.judgment: Strong and tightly scoped source audit. At 1,417 words it fits the 1,600-word ceiling and ranks four source-grounded hypotheses with exact file hashes/lines, contract risks, counterevidence, and minimum Main-only discriminating measurements.
scope_depth.evidence: It traces the startup gate, live owners, typed BF16 global storage, FP32 local score/softmax/accumulation, page bounds and source-declared work-group accounting. It distinguishes necessary storage/safety contracts from optional reduction and diagnostic work. It provides a pinned vLLM Xe2 design reference and marks its hardware and license limits.
scope_depth.limits: The report's opening statement that no current component profile attributes the delta is superseded by the newer coarse profile. The new profile windows remain nonexclusive, so they locate a candidate path but do not prove exclusive device service or isolate a source-level cause. No source inspection proves runtime, correctness, or numerical quality.

novelty_and_redundancy.judgment: Distinct from R787/R818's earlier general/native16-QSA reviews and R822/R824's low-precision norm/activation scope: R843 targets the exact current typed-QSA versus retained-FP32 source path and ranked potential costs. It avoids another generic attention survey.
novelty_and_redundancy.conclusion: Decision-support report is actionable selectively; it does not justify code changes by itself.

next_scopes.title: Event-time attribution for nonexclusive SYCL and Level Zero queue profiles
next_scopes.finite_question: Using official SYCL, Unified Runtime, Level Zero and Intel profiler documentation plus original studies, compare what SYCL event profiling timestamps, Level Zero event timestamps and one system trace actually time. How do host submission, device execution, dependencies, overlapping queues, clock domains, and profiling overhead affect sums and critical-path interpretation? Give one minimal evidence plan that separates per-command device duration, host submission gaps, and whole-request critical path without treating queue-window totals as exclusive GPU service.
next_scopes.breadth_and_counterevidence: Compare two or three concrete timestamp/trace mechanisms with exact runtime or tool versions, support requirements, overhead and failure modes. Include counterevidence where event duration does not equal end-to-end latency or cannot be summed across overlap. Keep this to timing semantics and attribution; exclude generic profiler recipes, kernel optimization proposals and Strata hardware performance claims.
next_scopes.report_budget: 1,300–1,700 substantive words; at most seven primary URLs; source revisions, measurement boundaries, applicability and evidence limits.
next_scopes.prerequisites: Public-source comparison only. Share the research index, this review, own-vllm-coarse-comparison-v1.json, and only the relevant R843 source-accounting and profile-update sections. Do not read R842's knowledge-collection body or run local profiling.
next_scopes.prerequisite_evidence: The current profile explicitly marks queue windows nonexclusive and inclusive of host submission gaps while comparing typed-QSA and retained-FP32 attention. The recorded intervals show 33.9610 versus 36.2963 seconds, but do not isolate device service time. R817's metadata concerns binary/ISA extraction; R842 concerns command-DAG replay; neither answers event-time attribution semantics.
next_scopes.novelty_guard: Focus on timestamp definitions, overlap and attribution boundaries. Do not repeat R842's graph capture/replay break-even survey or R843's source audit.
